memory_update.text: EAT is a high-signal operator mapping for casual-dining value, Chili's traffic, menu simplification, and margin durability; validate through traffic/price/mix and promotion intensity.

PAR and OLO are the purest restaurant-technology mappings in this chunk; PAR has broader POS/engagement/hardware exposure, while OLO is more concentrated in ordering, payments, delivery orchestration, and guest engagement.

MIDD maps to restaurant capex, throughput, kitchen automation, beverage, and refrigeration equipment, but restaurant-specific exposure must be separated from other commercial and institutional foodservice demand.

QSR, DPZ, WING, and WEN should be tracked as franchised-system unit-economics reads rather than only consumer-demand reads; key variables are franchisee margins, remodel obligations, traffic, price/mix, and net unit growth.
USFD is a broadline foodservice-distribution mapping; independent restaurant case volume is a useful proxy for restaurant demand and operator health.

BROS and SHAK are growth-concept mappings: BROS tests beverage frequency and drive-thru throughput, while SHAK tests premium fast-casual traffic, beef/labor cost pressure, and restaurant-level margin improvement.

WBT should be removed from the active public ticker universe because Welbilt is no longer a standalone public company after the Ali Group acquisition; rebuild the equipment node using active listed peers.

Need market-pricing checks for all tickers before prioritization: forward EV/EBITDA or P/E, same-store-sales expectations, estimate revisions, short interest, and relative performance versus restaurant and supplier peers.

Need a common restaurant KPI table across operator tickers: traffic, average check, price/mix, comparable sales, restaurant-level margin, labor cost, food/paper cost, net unit growth, franchised mix, and franchisee health indicators.

summary: Mapped ticker relationships for the candidate restaurant chunk across demand-facing restaurant operators, restaurant technology suppliers, foodservice distribution, and commercial kitchen equipment. Stronger public-market mappings: EAT as casual-dining traffic/value read-through; PAR and OLO as restaurant software/digital infrastructure; MIDD as commercial foodservice equipment; QSR, DPZ, WING, WEN as franchise-system unit economics and value/QSR traffic reads; USFD as distributor demand and food-cost-control node; BROS and SHAK as higher-growth concept tests for throughput, traffic, input costs, and restaurant-level margin. WBT should be removed or treated as a stale mapping because Welbilt is no longer a current public ticker after Ali Group's acquisition.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate FY2026 traffic versus price/mix decomposition, Chili's promotion intensity, Maggiano's turnaround metrics, restaurant-level margin, and commodity/labor cost commentary in the next 10-Q and earnings call.
ticker_relationships.node: consumer value, casual-dining traffic, menu engineering
ticker_relationships.relationship: Brinker is a direct demand-side relationship to the Restaurants theme through Chili's and Maggiano's. Its current relevance is highest as a read-through on whether value offers, advertising, simplified operations, and menu innovation can sustain casual-dining traffic and comparable sales without excessive margin sacrifice.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check ARR growth, net retention, customer wins/losses, implementation backlog, gross margin, cash burn, and competitive displacement versus Toast, NCR Voyix, Oracle, Olo, and in-house systems.
ticker_relationships.node: restaurant operating system software, POS, loyalty, ordering, payments
ticker_relationships.relationship: PAR is a focused restaurant-technology supplier tied to cloud POS, engagement/loyalty, ordering, hardware, and payment infrastructure. The relationship is supply-chain/infrastructure rather than restaurant traffic itself; it maps to the chokepoint question of whether operators continue funding digital systems to improve throughput, personalization, and labor productivity.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Separate restaurant-chain demand from institutional, convenience, lodging, and non-restaurant demand; track Commercial Foodservice Equipment orders, backlog, margins, dealer inventory, and tariff/steel exposure.
ticker_relationships.node: commercial kitchen, beverage, refrigeration, and automation equipment
ticker_relationships.relationship: Middleby maps to the restaurant capex and productivity node through commercial foodservice equipment, including cooking, beverage, warming, refrigeration, and automation-related product lines. Its relationship is indirect but important: if restaurant operators prioritize speed, labor efficiency, drive-thru throughput, and remodel/new-unit buildouts, MIDD can be a supplier read-through.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate comparable sales by brand and geography, net restaurant growth, franchisee profitability, remodel obligations, advertising support, and any stress among large franchisees.
ticker_relationships.node: global QSR franchisor, franchisee unit economics, value traffic, coffee and chicken/burger dayparts
ticker_relationships.relationship: Restaurant Brands International maps to global franchised QSR demand and franchise economics via Burger King, Tim Hortons, Popeyes, and Firehouse Subs. It is a useful cross-segment read-through for value menus, coffee frequency, chicken demand, burger/beef pressure, remodel funding, and international unit growth.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track independent restaurant case volume, chain volume, gross profit per case, private-label penetration, customer retention, acquisition contribution, and commentary on operator stress or menu substitution.
ticker_relationships.node: foodservice distribution, independent restaurant demand, food-cost management
ticker_relationships.relationship: US Foods maps to the broadline distribution node. Its independent-restaurant case volume is a high-signal demand indicator, while its exclusive brands and procurement capabilities connect to operator food-cost control and menu-engineering needs.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify U.S. same-store sales drivers, transaction versus ticket mix, digital order share, aggregator impact, franchisee cash-on-cash returns, supply-chain margin, and international master-franchise health.
ticker_relationships.node: pizza delivery/carryout, franchise economics, digital ordering, supply chain
ticker_relationships.relationship: Domino's maps directly to delivery and carryout restaurant demand, franchised store economics, digital ordering adoption, and vertically integrated pizza supply-chain exposure. It is a strong bellwether for value-oriented frequency and the competitive boundary between owned digital channels and third-party aggregators.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check domestic same-store sales, transaction counts, AUVs, franchisee restaurant-level margin, net openings, digital mix, advertising efficiency, and wing cost pass-through.
ticker_relationships.node: franchised chicken QSR, digital sales, unit growth, chicken-wing commodity exposure
ticker_relationships.relationship: Wingstop maps to the asset-light franchised growth node and to protein-cost sensitivity through chicken wings. Its high franchised mix and digital orientation make it a useful read-through for whether high-growth QSR concepts can keep unit economics attractive during traffic normalization and commodity-cost volatility.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate U.S. same-restaurant sales, traffic, breakfast availability and sales contribution, franchisee closures/openings, beef-cost commentary, and remodel/new-unit funding.
ticker_relationships.node: QSR value menus, franchisee economics, beef exposure, breakfast/daypart expansion
ticker_relationships.relationship: Wendy's maps to QSR traffic, value competition, beef-cost exposure, and franchise economics. Its breakfast/daypart initiatives and fresh-beef positioning make it a useful but potentially pressured node if consumer affordability and beef prices remain key constraints.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track same-shop transaction growth, drive-thru wait times, new-shop productivity, labor as a percentage of shop revenue, coffee/dairy input inflation, mobile order adoption, and cannibalization in new markets.
ticker_relationships.node: drive-thru coffee and beverage frequency, unit growth, throughput
ticker_relationships.relationship: Dutch Bros maps to beverage-led restaurant growth and drive-thru throughput. Its relationship is demand-side and operating-model focused: shop expansion, same-shop transactions, labor model, and coffee/input costs test whether beverage frequency can outperform broader restaurant traffic weakness.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate traffic versus price/mix, FY2026 restaurant-level margin, beef and labor headwinds, new-unit returns, urban versus suburban performance, and digital/channel mix.
ticker_relationships.node: premium fast casual, restaurant-level margin, traffic and beef exposure
ticker_relationships.relationship: Shake Shack maps to premium fast-casual demand and margin recovery. It is useful for testing the upper boundary of consumer pricing power in burgers, the effect of beef/labor inflation, and whether operational improvements can lift restaurant-level margins while the company opens new units.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check active locations, average revenue per unit, module penetration, gross merchandise volume, gross payment volume, churn, large-brand wins/losses, and overlap with PAR, Toast, DoorDash, Uber, Oracle, and NCR Voyix.
ticker_relationships.node: restaurant digital ordering, payments, delivery channel management, guest engagement
ticker_relationships.relationship: Olo maps to restaurant-specific digital infrastructure for ordering, payments, delivery coordination, catering, loyalty/marketing, and guest engagement. Its relationship is high-purity but needs competitive validation because restaurant brands can use in-house systems, POS vendors, delivery marketplaces, or broader payment platforms.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Confirm current listing status in market data and rebuild the equipment node using active public tickers, including MIDD and any other currently listed commercial foodservice equipment, refrigeration, beverage, or automation suppliers.
ticker_relationships.node: commercial foodservice equipment stale ticker mapping
ticker_relationships.relationship: WBT is not a valid current public-market mapping for Welbilt exposure. Welbilt was acquired by Ali Group and should be removed from the active public ticker universe or replaced with current public peers/suppliers such as MIDD where appropriate.
